bug_description.normalized: The staged witness saved as `gt_results/arvo_66063/poc` reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` on the invalid UTF-8 -> UTF-32 path in `roundtrip`. In `fuzz/roundtrip.cc`, `FuzzedDataProvider` first materializes an attacker-controlled `source` string, and `validate_utf8(source.c_str(), source.size())` is false on the crashing run, so the harness still executes `utf32_length_from_utf8` and `convert_utf8_to_utf32` on malformed input. The saved allocation stack shows that this invalid branch allocated 4068 bytes, i.e. 1017 `char32_t` slots, at `roundtrip.cc:173`. On the staged machine runtime dispatch selects `simdutf::haswell::implementation::convert_utf8_to_utf32`, even though the public issue's crash state named westmere; both architectures share the vulnerable generic safety-margin code in `src/generic/utf8_to_utf32/utf8_to_utf32.h`, and the staged patch fixes that shared code. The vulnerable converter scans backward from the end counting only four trailing leading bytes to derive `safety_margin`, even though the adjacent comment and Haswell helper implementation show that `convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32` may physically overstore 4 or 8 extra bytes near malformed tail data. That underestimated margin keeps the SIMD loop active too deep into the tail, lets the masked helper consume the missing output slack, and leaves a later all-ASCII window to reach `store_ascii_as_utf32` with too little headroom. AddressSanitizer then catches a `WRITE of size 32` 3 bytes past the 4068-byte heap allocation. The staged fix closes this bug by increasing the backward scan from 4 to 8 leading bytes in both `convert` and `convert_with_errors`, and the patch adds `convert_invalid_special_cases` to cover the same invalid-input length-then-convert contract.

source.description: First project-side materialization on the crashing path. The fuzz target consumes attacker-controlled bytes from `FuzzedDataProvider` into the `source` string that later feeds UTF-8 validation, UTF-32 length prediction, and UTF-32 conversion.
source.value_from: The exact staged corpus `gt_results/arvo_66063/poc` is passed as `(data, size)` to `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and this statement is the first project statement that turns those bytes into the vulnerability-relevant `source` object. The saved crash later proves that this materialized string took the invalid UTF-8 branch and led to the 1017-word `utf32_output` allocation at `roundtrip.cc:173`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The vulnerable converter counts only four trailing leading bytes when deriving `safety_margin`, even though the Haswell `convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32` helper can overstore 4 or 8 bytes past its logical UTF-32 output near malformed tail data. On invalid UTF-8, the underestimated margin fails to reserve that helper slack before later SIMD writes.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes both `leading_byte < 4` sites in `convert` and `convert_with_errors` to `leading_byte < 8`, matching the adjacent comment that the Haswell masked helper may need up to 8 bytes of extra output slack.

sink.description: Sink. This AVX store in the later Haswell ASCII fast path becomes the first observed out-of-bounds write after the earlier masked-helper tail slack has been exhausted.
sink.note: AddressSanitizer reports the generated singleheader equivalent at `/src/simdutf/build/singleheader/simdutf.cpp:1770:7` with a `WRITE of size 32` at `0x621000004ce7`, 3 bytes past the 4068-byte region allocated at `roundtrip.cc:173`. The crash is observed here rather than inside the masked helper because this is the next wide store after the missing tail headroom has been consumed.

tainted_value_origin.description: Attacker-controlled bytes first become the vulnerability-relevant `source` string at this statement. That string is then validated, length-counted, and converted on the crashing invalid UTF-8 -> UTF-32 path.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crash later reaches the invalid-input UTF-32 allocation and conversion at `roundtrip.cc:170-177`, so this validation result was false and the harness took the corresponding `else` arm for the same `source` string.

dispatch_arm.code: simdutf_warn_unused size_t implementation::convert_utf8_to_utf32(const char* buf, size_t len, char32_t* utf32_output) const noexcept {
dispatch_arm.description: The staged ASan trace and `reproduction_report.json` both show that runtime dispatch selected the Haswell implementation on this machine, so the shared generic transcoder reached the Haswell ASCII store sink.

evidence_limitations: The prepared simdutf checkout reviewed in Stage 02 is local commit `59b81c798c0c88ca4c573ebde77c3b38eb0352cb`, not metadata commit `9504bf8e7a6aa0a752173a3e83084b31af1a39bb`. The trace therefore cites exact lines from the staged snapshot whose vulnerable hunk matches the minus side of the staged `patch.diff`.

The public OSS-Fuzz issue named `simdutf::westmere::implementation::convert_utf8_to_utf32`, but the staged reproduction on this runtime dispatched to `simdutf::haswell::implementation::convert_utf8_to_utf32`. The vulnerable `src/generic/utf8_to_utf32/utf8_to_utf32.h` safety-margin logic patched by `c708a9e4c1dc880241c252bec76fada53ab84da3` is shared across those architecture implementations.

The staged static artifacts do not identify which `convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32` fast subcase executed before the crash. The trace therefore records only the source-grounded shared fact from `src/haswell/avx2_convert_utf8_to_utf32.cpp` that the helper can consume 4 or 8 bytes of physical headroom beyond its logical UTF-32 advance, not a stronger claim about which exact arm fired.

The staged static artifacts do not reconstruct the exact intermediate `source` string produced by `FuzzedDataProvider::ConsumeRandomLengthString(1024)` from the raw 2609-byte corpus. They establish only that the materialized string took the invalid UTF-8 branch, produced the observed 1017-word allocation at `roundtrip.cc:173`, and then hit the saved overflow.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz target materializes an attacker-controlled `source` string, validates it as UTF-8, and because that predicate is false on the crashing run it selects the invalid UTF-8 -> UTF-32 branch.

That invalid-input branch asks `utf32_length_from_utf8(source)` to count UTF-32 code points and allocates `utf32_output` from the result; ASan shows the destination extent is 1017 `char32_t` words (4068 bytes).

During `convert_utf8_to_utf32`, the shared generic converter scans backward for only four leading bytes, underestimates `safety_margin`, and keeps the SIMD loop alive too deep into malformed tail data.

Inside that extra tail region, the non-ASCII Haswell masked helper writes 16 or 32 physical bytes while advancing only 12 or 24 logical bytes, consuming the 4-8 bytes of slack that should have been reserved.
A later ASCII fast-path block uses the same pointer state, and the first AVX store in `store_ascii_as_utf32` lands 3 bytes past the 4068-byte heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: Source. The fuzz target materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the `source` string object that later flows through validation, length prediction, and UTF-32 conversion.

The harness derives `validutf8` from the materialized string and branches on it. The saved crash later at line 176 is only reachable when this predicate is false, so this `source` takes the invalid UTF-8 `else` arm instead of the valid round-trip arm.
Once the invalid branch is selected, the harness still asks simdutf to predict how many UTF-32 code points this malformed `source` would produce.

The length routine treats every byte outside the UTF-8 continuation range `0x80..0xBF` as a code-point boundary and returns that count as `expected_utf32words`. The later ASan allocation shows this count was 1017 on the crashing path.

The invalid-input branch allocates the destination buffer from step 4's count. AddressSanitizer attributes the overflowed heap object to this allocation and reports 4068 bytes, i.e. 1017 `char32_t` slots.

fine_trace.code:
size_t utf32words = e->convert_utf8_to_utf32(
    source.c_str(), source.size(), utf32_output.get());
fine_trace.note: The same malformed `source` string and the fixed-size `utf32_output` buffer are passed into the vulnerable UTF-8-to-UTF-32 converter.

Root cause. The converter derives its trailing safety margin by scanning backward only until it has seen four leading bytes. On malformed UTF-8 that understates the 4-8 bytes of output headroom the Haswell masked helper may need near the tail.

The converter uses the underestimated `safety_margin` as its loop stop condition. On the crashing path this predicate stays true deeper into the malformed tail, so blocks that should have been left to trailing scalar/error handling remain eligible for more SIMD work.
On a non-ASCII 64-byte block that step 8 still admits, the converter computes a code-point-end mask and repeatedly calls `convert_masked_utf8_to_utf32` with the live `utf32_output` pointer.

The Haswell helper's fast subcases store wider vectors than their logical UTF-32 advance: one path writes 32 bytes but advances by only 24 logical bytes, and another writes 16 bytes but advances by only 12 logical bytes. This consumes the 4-8 bytes of physical headroom that step 7 failed to reserve near the tail.

Later in the still-admitted tail region, a 64-byte block satisfies `input.is_ascii()`, so conversion switches to the ASCII fast path using the `utf32_output` state after step 10 has already consumed the missing slack.

Sink. The first 32-byte AVX store of the ASCII expansion lands beyond the heap buffer created at step 5. AddressSanitizer reports this write at `0x621000004ce7`, 3 bytes past the 4068-byte region `[0x621000003d00, 0x621000004ce4)` allocated at `roundtrip.cc:173`.

allocation_context.note: ASan attributes the overflowed heap region to `new char32_t[expected_utf32words]` in the invalid-input branch. The reported region size is 4068 bytes, which corresponds to 1017 UTF-32 words.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, staged patch.diff, and the prepared simdutf snapshot

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The overflowed object is the invalid-branch `utf32_output` buffer allocated after `validate_utf8(source)` returned false and `utf32_length_from_utf8(source)` returned 1017; the root cause is the later underestimation of the 4-8 bytes of tail headroom needed before the Haswell masked-helper and ASCII SIMD writes into that same buffer.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch fixes the shared generic source by increasing the backward scan from 4 to 8 leading bytes in both UTF-8-to-UTF-32 conversion variants, and it adds `convert_invalid_special_cases` to lock in the invalid-input length-then-convert regression.

format.name: saved libFuzzer corpus file consumed by `roundtrip`
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the exact 2609-byte corpus saved as `gt_results/arvo_66063/poc`. The verified trigger semantics from the staged run are only that `roundtrip` consumes this corpus, materializes a `source` string via `ConsumeRandomLengthString(1024)`, `validate_utf8(source.c_str(), source.size())` is false, the invalid UTF-32 branch at `fuzz/roundtrip.cc:168-177` allocates 1017 `char32_t` words at line 173, and the later conversion exhausts the missing 4-8 bytes of tail headroom before AddressSanitizer catches the Haswell ASCII store. This contract stays at the saved witness and observed branch; it does not generalize that raw byte pattern to a broader input class or to a uniquely reconstructed intermediate string.
